notes: Overview: Mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) building an in-app product assistant (feature assistant) and embedding-powered search. Evaluated Hosted API in Sep-Oct 2024 (pooled usage) -> POC moved to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost isolation. POC summary: 2-week POC (Oct 10-24) using gpt-style open model from Redwood catalog; target 75ms p95 for short prompts, throughput 120 qps for embeddings indexing pipeline. Results: Hosted API met quality but saw spiky latency at peak ingestion; Dedicated infra candidate met latency SLO in 3/4 stress runs after KV caching enabled. Pricing discussion: initial Dedicated term proposed by RDW: 12-month commitment, 4 A100-equivalent slots steady, 2-slot burst for 2 hours/day peak, overage billed at 1.8x committed rate. AtlasHarbor counter: wants ramp schedule (3 -> 4 -> 6 slots over 6 months), lower burst multiplier (1.4x), and clear overage cap. They are cost-sensitive: CFO prefers predictable monthly commit caps. SE notes: caching and batch config reductions likely lower required committed capacity by ~20% after month 2. Security/compliance: require SSO/SAML, company-managed KMS, audit logging retention 1 year, EU data residency for EU customers. Legal: outstanding KMS DPA CLA language. Quotes from calls: "We need billing we can forecast into the product roadmap — unpredictable overages kill features." — Head of Platform. Next: AE to send revised term sheet with ramp schedule and detailed burst/overage calculator (see drive deck). Legal to sync with Redwood counsel on KMS excerpt by 2024-11-07. Contract owner wants pilot invoice at 25% commit for month 1. use_case_summary: Primary: in-product feature assistant (low latency, cost-sensitive). Secondary: embeddings for doc-search and reranking for personalized recommendations. Throughput/Latency: target 50-100 qps for assistant; p95 latency <= 100ms for prompts under 256 tokens; embeddings pipeline 120 qps, eventual bulk reindex nightly. SLAs wanted: 99.9% uptime, predictable tail latency. Model preference: customer open to Llama-style/Redwood-verified open models; cares about quantized 8-bit cost options and fallbacks to cheaper variants during degradation. Routing needs: regional routing EU/NA and fallback model variant on capacity constraints.
